The oak_wall_sign provides directional guidance (e.g., 'Workshop this way') leading the player toward the crafting area. Once the player has found both landmarks and navigated to the crafting area, they can craft a lever using a stick and cobblestone that are available there. This creates a natural exploration-then-craft progression that doesn't require deep Minecraft knowledge — just finding items and using a crafting table with provided materials.

The oak_wall_sign is at spawn-relative (2, 1, 0) on a fence post. max_distance reduced from 16 to 4 based on ValidatorAgent feedback — the sign is only ~2.24 blocks from spawn, so a large radius would trivially trigger. With max_distance=4 and facing_tolerance=60, the player must be close AND looking at the sign, preventing accidental completion from spawn without intentional observation.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The cauldron is at spawn-relative (10, 1, 3) inside the cobblestone workshop building. max_distance reduced from 16 to 6 based on ValidatorAgent feedback — this ensures the player must navigate to the building doorway (at x=7) or inside the building to trigger. From spawn (0,0,0), distance is ~10.49 (outside range). facing_tolerance=60 ensures the player is looking toward the cauldron.

Uses inventory_has because crafting a lever results in the item appearing in the player's inventory. The player crafts a lever from 1 stick + 1 cobblestone at the crafting table inside the workshop. No lever exists in the scene initially, so having min_count=1 confirms successful crafting.
